newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks tumble as Dow loses 100 pts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks tumble as Dow loses 100 pts.

text.p: European share markets, already weakened by profit-takers, took a late tumble on Friday as Wall Street fell more than 100 points.

Wall Street's slide below 8,000 points, provoked by disappointment over earnings from hi-tech companies, sent ripples into the foreign exchange markets where dealers vented their frustrations by pushing the dollar lower.

London stocks managed a quick spurt to within a whisker of the 5,000-point barrier in early trade. But the FTSE-100 index soon fell back and joined the continental markets, where investors cashed in on a string of record highs this week.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gave the sting in the tail of the trading week. Disappointment with earnings from Microsoft Corp triggered a reaction to the bull run which took the Dow over 8,000 points this week for the first time.

As London dealers went home, the Dow was down 125.9 points at 7,894.41 and still falling. Paris was the chief casualty among the leading European stock markets as investors fretted over possible company tax hikes aimed at fixing the French budget for European monetary union.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn is expected to announce on Monday (0800 GMT) a package aimed at cutting the public deficit, which is threatening to hit 3.6 percent of gross domestic product -- far above the 3.0 percent target for joining the single European currency.
Most of this year's measures are expected to be on the revenue side, with a "euro surcharge" on corporate tax expected to raise about 12 billion francs ($2 billion), officials said.
The thought of higher company taxes chilled the Paris bourse, which opened lower and fell most of the day. The CAC-40 index closed down 81.90 points (2.77 percent) at 2,876.69.

London managed a strong morning performance and the FTSE-100 index hit a record intraday high of 4,998.1. But for the third time this week the FTSE failed to break the 5,000 barrier and the buying, dictated largely by technical factors, faded away.
Wall Street accelerated the fall and the FTSE closed down 71.8 points or 1.45 percent at 4,877.2.

"The market has had a bout of the jitters...but a lot of fund managers have been on the wrong foot this year and will probably love the chance to buy in at lower levels," said one dealer. "But 5,000 seems to be a bit of a barrier and this sort of volatility is a bit frightening."

German shares, which closed at a record high on Thursday, also suffered from profit-taking. The DAX index of blue chips closed down 30.78 points or 0.73 percent at 4,196.53. The IBIS index, which measures post-bourse electronic trade, closed down 1.71 percent at 4,131.94.
Wall Street also put pressure on the dollar as traders vented their frustation that it failed to hold above the psychological 1.80 mark level.
The dollar was not helped by a 17 percent rise in the U.S. May trade deficit, and the fact that the deficit with Japan shrank 25 percent gave it only a brief lift against the yen.

"People have been trying to short the dollar all week above 1.80, and they've been cut out each time it's gone above there.. They're all fed up and primed to sell it on any move down," said Robin Poynder, chief dealer at Charterhouse in London.
The dollar hit a session low of 1.7856 marks before clawing back to 1.7892 in late trading, compared with late Thursday's European level of 1.7998.
It also was at an intraday low of 115.35 yen compared with its previous close of 116.07.

News that the U.S. trade deficit with Japan fell to $3.63 billion in May sent the dollar to a session high of 116.20 yen. But the market swiftly decided to focus instead on the larger than expected overall U.S. deficit of $10.23 billion.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 115.35 yen and 1.7892 marks compared with 115.35 yen and 1.7998 marks in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 71.8 points or 1.45 percent at 4,877.2 after hitting a record intradday high of 4,998.1.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade closed down 30.78 points or 0.73 percent at 4,196.53. The IBIS index, which measures post-bourse electronic trade, closed down 1.71 percent at 4,131.94.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 81.90 points (2.77 percent) at 2,876.69.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $324.15 an ounce, up $4.60. Silver was 11 cents higher at $4.30. ($ = 6.056 French Francs)
